text.title: Multi-Region Failover Pattern Pack Decision Tree

decision-tree.root-question: Are numeric RPO and RTO per workload tier agreed with the business owner and recorded as `rpo_minutes` and `rto_minutes`?

branch.conclusion: Stop. Get the two numbers per tier from the business owner first; no pattern can be chosen or costed without them.

branch.question: Does the workload actually run, or need to run, in more than one region (regulatory, RTO under what a single-region restore can deliver, or customer commitment)?

branch.conclusion: Skip this methodology. A single-region backup-and-restore plan with tested restores covers the requirement; a multi-region pack would be cost without a driver.

branch.question: Are database replication mode and measured p99 lag, object-store backfill status, and the region-scoped dependency list all recorded?

branch.conclusion: Collect the replication, backfill and dependency facts before choosing a pattern; the declared RPO is bounded by the measured lag.

branch.question: Has a live drill been run since the last change to replication, DNS or promotion, with measured RTO and RPO recorded?

branch.conclusion: Choose the pattern from RPO/RTO and cost, label the pack `unverified`, and schedule the drill that turns it into a verified pack.
Produce the full pack: pattern with achievable vs required RPO/RTO, DNS mechanics, database and object-store sections, dependency list, drill results and failback procedure.

example.p: Payments tier: RPO 5 min, RTO 30 min agreed. Multi-region required by RTO. Async Postgres replication with 12 s p99 lag, S3 backfill job cited, IdP confirmed multi-region. No drill since the DNS health check changed → r-drill-live-with-measured-results: pack labelled `unverified`, drill scheduled on 5% of traffic.
